assignmentHtml.task:
全面调查 J House jr. 的 YouTube 频道。查明以下事项：

  1. 稳定频道 ID 及规范 URL。
  2. 运营方／创作者：谁在运营该频道？巴西家庭。
  3. 频道创建日期，以及目前仍公开的最早上传视频。
  4. 运营地点及频道显示的国家。
  5. 使用的语言（葡萄牙语）。
  6. 主要内容类别（儿童／家庭）。
  7. 内容供应模式。
  8. 代表性系列。提供直接来源 URL。
assignmentHtml.context: 根据 Communitrics 于 2026 年 9 月 2 日的快照，J House jr. 排名第 35 名，历史累计观看量约为 61B（610 亿）次。需要可核实的事实，并附来源链接。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 一份关于 J House jr. 的结构化资料，包含全部要求的字段，每个字段均附来源 URL。

answerHtml:
J House jr. Dossier — Key findings with source-backed corrections

(1) Stable channel ID and canonical URL

  • Channel ID: UC57LcmyyZGQ2azPREsxwWSw
  • Canonical handle URL: https://www.youtube.com/@jhousejr. (per Wikipedia's most-viewed channels list)
  • Legacy channel URL: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC57LcmyyZGQ2azPREsxwWSw

(2) Operator/creator

  • Run by parents Kendra and Jeremy Johnston, a homeschooling couple based in Kansas City, Missouri, USA, with five children: Isaac, Elise, Caleb, Laura, and Janae. J House Vlogs is their original vlog channel (started 2014); J House jr. is the kids-focused spinoff.
  • IMPORTANT CORRECTION: This is an American family, not a Brazilian family, and the language is English, not Portuguese. No evidence supports any Brazilian or Portuguese-language connection.

(3) Channel creation date and earliest still-public upload

  • Channel created: June 1, 2019 (Social Blade; TubeLeader)
  • Spinoff announced Nov 3, 2019, then shelved indefinitely due to YouTube's COPPA kids-content policy until August 2021 (Wikitubia/J House Vlogs fandom page)
  • Earliest confirmed still-public upload: 🎃Trick-or-Treat🎃 uploaded October 22, 2021 (7.9M views) and 🎃Trick-or-Treating🎃 uploaded October 23, 2021 (33.6M views, likely the channel's most-viewed video)
  • Note: The gap between channel creation (June 2019) and first uploads (~October 2021) reflects the COPPA delay.

(4) Operating location and displayed country

  • United States (Kansas City, Missouri). Wikipedia lists country as "United States"; HypeAuditor and CreatorDB also list United States.

(5) Languages

  • English. Wikipedia lists primary language as English; CreatorDB states "Posts in English." No Portuguese content found.

(6) Primary content category

  • Wikipedia classifies it as "Entertainment" (rank #37 among most-viewed channels globally, 58.4B views at snapshot date)
  • HypeAuditor classifies it as "Family & Parenting" (rank #71 US, 36M subscribers, 61.5B views)
  • CreatorDB describes it as kids-focused family content within the family/kids space
  • air.io describes it as a "family-oriented channel" focused on safe, entertaining content for young viewers

(7) Content supply model

  • High-volume original kids' entertainment publisher model: ~8,700 videos, ~36M subscribers, ~61.5B lifetime views. Output centers on original music videos (upbeat, simple-concept productions), plus challenges, educational segments, and sponsored family experiences (Disney Cruise Line voyages, DreamWorks partnerships). Upload cadence is very high (~1 video/day, ~34 videos/month per Social Blade). Revenue estimated $215K–$3.4M/month (Social Blade).

(8) Representative series

  • Debut album "Come and Play" series including: "Come and Play" (music video), "Rock Paper Scissors," "Go Outside," "Chips and Salsa" — all full music videos produced for young audiences (CreatorDB)
  • Trick-or-Treating/Trick-or-Treat series (highest-viewed video: 33.6M views)
  • Hide-N-Seek/Sardines challenge series
  • Regular holiday specials (Christmas, Halloween) and family adventure highlights repurposed from J House Vlogs

(9) Key metrics snapshot

  • ~35.9M–36M subscribers; ~61.5B cumulative views; 8,700+ videos (Social Blade data through Sept 17, 2026)
  • Ranked #37 globally by total views per Wikipedia; Communitrics snapshot (Sept 2, 2026) placed #35 with ~61B lifetime views — consistent with the trajectory
  • Blown up significantly in May 2024 (air.io)

(10) Corrections to orchestrator's assumed context

  • NOT a Brazilian family; they are American (Kansas City, Missouri)
  • Language is English, NOT Portuguese
  • Category conflict: Wikipedia says "Entertainment" while HypeAuditor says "Family & Parenting" — both labels appear in use across sources
